verdict.rationale: Mercury's own API covers a broad slice of what the UI does: accounts and balances, transactions and metadata, categories, attachments, statements, treasury, cards (issue, limits, lifecycle), payments over ACH, check, domestic and international wire, internal transfers, approval requests, invoices and customers, and webhooks. A CLI and MCP server sit on top of it. However, nothing documents full UI parity, and some flows are explicitly dashboard-bound: API-queued disbursements are signed off in the dashboard, and access revocation is done from the dashboard. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity claim, API coverage of user/permission management, reimbursements, bill pay, accounting sync and account opening, API-side approval/sign-off, and independent hands-on corroboration of coverage breadth.
